title: Echo Moon
research_question: What would happen in real physics if a pyramid system were aligned with the Moon, used a gold or electrum apex as a converter/reflector, entered its own acoustic resonance, illuminated its casing, and nearby obelisks caught and redirected the lunar light onward?

scenario_boundary.rule: Model what is physically possible without converting the hypothesis into a historical fact.

exemplar_geometry.note: The Great Pyramid dimensions and casing are used as an engineering exemplar. A gold/electrum capstone for Khufu is not treated as established evidence.

lunar_alignment_gate.why_not_exact_nadir_for_optics: When the Moon is geometrically below the site, Earth blocks direct lunar light. Nadir remains relevant only to the tidal axis.
lunar_alignment_gate.upper_and_lower_tidal_symmetry: The lunar tidal axis is near an extremum both overhead and underfoot; the upper case is selected because it also supplies direct moonlight.
lunar_alignment_gate.interpretation: Near a major lunar standstill, the Moon can approach the local vertical at Giza closely enough that the tidal-axis geometry is essentially maximal while direct moonlight is available. Exact coincidence with full phase is a timing condition, not assumed.

tidal_physics_run.reason: The lunar forcing is millions of times slower than 119 Hz. A passive linear stone structure cannot frequency-upconvert this slow tidal drive into a sustained 119 Hz acoustic oscillation by resonance alone.

gold_or_electrum_apex_model.historical_analogy: Gold/electrum-clad obelisk pyramidions are historically attested in New Kingdom contexts; this supports the material choice as reflective monumental technology, not the Khufu lunar-converter claim.

photoelectric_check.interpretation: Visible moonlight is below the clean-gold photoelectric threshold. Gold can reflect and conduct, but a strong electrical power channel would require another material, UV-sensitive process, stored charge, or other energy mechanism.

whole_pyramid_moonlight_run.interpretation: A white, smooth limestone casing under a high full Moon could look strikingly luminous against a dark desert and cast/refine shadows, but it would not illuminate the surroundings like sunlight. The total incident light is spread over a huge area.

ideal_specular_pyramidion_raytrace.assumption: A hypothetical metal-coated apex face continues the Great Pyramid face slope and behaves approximately as a flat mirror.
ideal_specular_pyramidion_raytrace.incident_case: Moon approximately overhead; incident rays approximately vertical
ideal_specular_pyramidion_raytrace.formula: beta = 2 * face_slope - 90 degrees; ground_range ~= height / tan(beta)
ideal_specular_pyramidion_raytrace.four_face_interpretation: Four facets can create four moving specular sectors around the pyramid. Near-zenith lunar motion shifts the footprint with time rather than producing a stationary ring.

obelisk_optical_relay.historical_material_basis: Ancient Egyptian obelisk tips could be sheathed in gold or electrum and were explicitly associated with catching/reflection of sunlight.
obelisk_optical_relay.flat_mirror_minimum_source_limited_beam_: approximately the Moon's 0.5 degree angular diameter, before surface roughness and alignment error

same_photon_multihop_chain.reason: Every hop expands to a Moon-sized angular patch and the next finite pyramidion intercepts only part of that patch, in addition to reflectivity and alignment losses.

physically_better_network_interpretation.description: Each obelisk is already illuminated by the Moon and can redirect its own incident lunar light toward a next site when geometry is correct. A glint from the previous node can serve as timing/alignment evidence rather than carrying all optical energy through the entire chain.

acoustic_activation_model.hard_requirement: The acoustic energy must come from an energy store/source. Lunar gravity and moonlight can provide timing/alignment signals but are far too weak and slow to be assumed as the sole power source for a large 119 Hz acoustic event.

testable_predictions: Ray-trace reconstructed apex facets at lunar standstill declinations and search for repeated ground-intersection corridors near predicted reflection sectors.
Compare candidate obelisk positions and surviving temple axes against specular reflection solutions rather than broad symbolic alignments.
Search original pyramidion/obelisk surfaces for metal cladding attachment traces, conductive continuity, intentional electrical isolation, or mounting features; treat absence as negative evidence.
Measure whether any chamber or structural modes couple strongly to the 117-121 Hz project band; do not infer tuning from coincidence alone.
Model direct Moon illumination at every candidate node. Prefer the direct-moon-per-node network over same-photon multihop if both fit the geometry.
Preserve lunar phase, declination, atmospheric extinction, surface roughness and facet orientation as explicit variables in any archaeological ray-trace.

sources.claim: Great Pyramid original height 146.5 m and high-quality Tura limestone casing

Hatshepsut obelisks were described as gilded with large amounts of fine gold

Moon angular diameter is about 0.5 degree

Lunar tidal day 24 h 50 min and semidiurnal high-tide spacing about 12 h 25 min

Modeled brightest full-moon ground illuminance can approach approximately 0.36 lux under favorable conditions
Measured clean-gold work function approximately 5.30-5.45 eV

scientific_boundary.MODEL_RESULT: A lunar-timed optical and active acoustic system is physically constructible in principle, but passive moonlight/tidal forcing alone cannot power or frequency-drive a large 119 Hz pyramid resonance.
